text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Nokia will not move its headquarters abroad and is staying in Finland for the time being, CEO Jorma Ollila says.
- There should be more cuts in state spending, current 2003 target date to halt growth in national debt is too late, Iiro Viinanen, insurer Pohjola's CEO says.
- Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says he will not stay on as Conservative party chairman after 1999. @
- MPs slammed "Natura 2000", Ministry of Environment's EU programme, as too protective and a threat to the economy.
- Energy group Teollisuuden Voima plans to increase capacity of current nuclear plants, because it is not allowed to build any new ones.
- U.S. broadcasting company ABC broadcast its morning news from Helsinki, showing Finland through sauna, tango, boot- throwing and wife-carrying competitions.
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen played role of president for five minutes on Thursday, deputising for Martti Ahtisaari while he is away in South Africa. @
AAMULEHTI
- Economic outlook seems positive for metal industry, but the sector is troubled by diversity, representative says.
- Aamulehti starts training programme for journalists.
- Social Democrats want to change electoral districts in line with changes made to provinces.
- Obesity may be hereditary, professor says.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Newspaper advertising increased last year by a couple of percent. @
- Focus in construction is moving into apartment building; sector will create 15,000 new jobs this year, state secretary Mauno Saari says.
- Social and Health Affairs Ministry is not planning to abolish state compensation for private doctor visits, Minister Sirkka Monkare says in response to doctors' assertions.
- Homosexuals and their rights were only parts of a game in rivalry between liberals and conservatives, says theologian, discussing old dispute in the Finnish church. @
DEMARI
- Finnish language should be given minority-language status in Sweden as Swedish has in Finland, EU Minister Ole Norrback says.
HUFVUDSTADBLADET
- Report on "Estonia" disaster delayed -- not due out until midsummer, committee says.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
